home.title: INSPECT

headline.suffix: what is truly happening in your application.

home.content: INSPECT is a platform for monitoring and analyzing multiple types of calls and designed to provide deep visibility into the interactions between different components of a distributed system. INSPECT allows you to monitor and analyze the performance of your application, identify potential issues, and optimize your system's performance.

cta.title: Ready to transform your observability and a lot more?
cta.subtitle: Integrate INSPECT easily and get total visibility over your microservices in minutes.

profiles.title: Who is INSPECT for ?
profiles.description: At first look, you might think that INSPECT is a developer tool only. But its value comes from the fact that every profile can use it. Developers are indeed the ones that have to implement it in the code. But after the implementation, everyone will find their work easier by using it.

technical.title: Technical profile
technical.content: Technical profiles can check the health of microservices, if the deployment has errors. INSPECT can also be used for log analysis, to find the root cause of an issue. Many protocols are unified to avoid a long search in multiple log files.

description.first: Quick diagnosis and root cause isolation
description.second: Monitoring the health of deployments and versions
description.third: Centralization and unification of heterogeneous logs

functional.title: Functional profile
functional.content: A functional profile might be able to find out easily what is wrong without asking the dev team to check for logs because INSPECT provides detailed informations. It is also possible to see which requests are the most used and which are the most critical, helping to prioritize the backlog.

description.first: Clear visibility on business flows without technical expertise
description.second: Identification of the most used requests and services
description.third: Informed backlog prioritization based on real data

redirect.profiles: More details on the use cases

description.description: A full package of tools in order to supervise, understand, and improve your application performances.

observability.title: Observability
observability.content: INSPECT is a tool that can facilitate the observability of your application. It allows you to detect and diagnose problems in complex systems. You have optimal observability on your application.

metrics.title: Metrics
metrics.content: INSPECT allows you to extract useful insights from the collected data. This helps understand trends, identify queries more effectively, and improve system performance.

time.title: Real time
time.content: INSPECT allows you to follow in real time the API calls and the global performances. It helps for detecting quickly some issues and to resolve them before your users are getting impacted from it

e2e.title: Start to end informations
e2e.content: When you are trying to find the root cause of an issue, you might be used to look for one log in a lot of files and lines. INSPECT makes you improve time because it's able to follow an action to it's start until it's end, even if the trace id are changing.

uniformize.title: Data uniformization
uniformize.content: Request analyzed are uniformized at a maximum level. If the callback are HTTP requests, JDBC, SMTP... The responses are studied so you can understand easily where the issue is located, even without any technical knowledge.

heartbeat.title: Monitoring
heartbeat.content: With INSPECT, you can watch and monitor all microservices of your project, know when was the last restart, what is the deployed version, the number of restarts, all of it in a few seconds.

features.title: INSPECT : a tool for telemetry, observability, and monitoring
features.subtitle: Total visibility for technical and functional teams, with zero code modifications.

observability.title: Observability
observability.subtitle: Understanding internal system state through external signals
observability.description: Observability is the ability to understand a software system's internal health, behavior, and failures simply by analyzing its external outputs.

value.title: What it brings to you:
value.desc: No more crisis meetings where teams blame each other. Observability enables everyone (business, support, developers) to understand within seconds what truly happened during an incident.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.subtitle: Automatic and continuous collection of vital signals
telemetry.description: Telemetry refers to the automated collection of raw measurements and signals from the core of your applications: execution times, errors encountered, memory consumption, or the journey taken by a transaction.

value.title: What it brings to you:
value.desc: Telemetry provides objective, indisputable facts. You no longer rely on assumptions: every user action or nightly batch job has a timestamped factual record.

solution.title: INSPECT unifies these two principles
solution.subtitle: The universal bridge between technical reality and business stakes
solution.description: INSPECT gathers all telemetry, transforming it instantly into clear, visual observability.

points.observability: Observability: you can observe the health of your services through INSPECT. You can tell immediately if some requests are failing.
points.telemetry: Telemetry: you have access to all the telemetry data, like execution time, errors, and memory consumption.

intro.subtitle: Continuous visibility into your application health
intro.description: Monitoring an application means keeping a constant watch on its state. INSPECT automatically detects every event (success or failure), execution speed metric, and anomaly, correlating business events with their technical traces.

traces.title: Execution traces
traces.description: The complete chronological journey of a request across the application, step by step.
traces.benefit: Know exactly where and why a transaction slowed down or failed.

metrics.title: Performance metrics
metrics.description: Periodic numerical indicators: average execution latency, request volume.
metrics.benefit: Assess overall application health and plan future capacity needs.

exceptions.title: Exceptions and errors
exceptions.description: Exceptions and errors are detected and logged with details to understand fully an anomaly
exceptions.benefit: Being able to make a diagnosis without technical skills, just by knowing how your application works functionnaly.

dualtrace.title: Dual Event Trace
dualtrace.description: Event trace is possible between multiple applications no matter if there are multiple protocols involved.
dualtrace.benefit: Instant shared understanding between business and technical teams.

events.title: Events and execution contexts
events.subtitle: API, BATCH, Startup, Tests: understanding all forms of system activity
events.description: An application doesn't limit itself at only a few clicks and some pop-ups. There are, almost always, a lot of batchs and tasks in background or during the night who are necessary and need to be monitored

batch.title: Web requests and regular tasks
batch.desc: Every application executes web requests, using API. But there are also batchs jobs, who execute synchronously tasks, as for example deleting old datas every month or every year. These APIs and these batches can be monitored by INSPECT.

startup.title: Startup & Initialization
startup.desc: The moment the application boots up, connects to databases, and loads configurations. INSPECT highlights components causing slow boot times.

tests.title: Automated Tests
tests.desc: Automated checks run before releasing to production. INSPECT detects performance regressions and bugs during staging.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams

first.title: Total visibility into batches
first.desc: Never discover too late that some task failed at 3 AM. INSPECT gives you full status, duration, and the exact failing item.

second.title: Instant API diagnostics
second.desc: Instantly pinpoint whether latency comes from your server, the network, or a third-party partner service.

third.title: Continuous quality validation
third.desc: Compare performance between releases during QA tests to prevent regressions from reaching production.

workflow.title: Outbound flows and system dependencies
workflow.subtitle: Multi protocols
workflow.description: No application lives in isolation. It's complicated to have a unique method to analyze all flows because there is no unique exchange protocol. There are multiples. INSPECT takes in consideration this issue by handling multiple protocols.

jdbc.title: JDBC / Database
jdbc.desc: INSPECT can read and analyze queries executed in your database. If transactions take time, it becomes easily noticeable and actions can be taken (such as adding indexes).

rest.title: HTTP Requests
rest.desc: Monitor calls to partner applications. Response codes are taken into account (200, 400, 500...)

ftp.title: FTP / SFTP
ftp.desc: Sending or fetching files from remote servers. INSPECT monitors throughput, file sizes, and network connection errors.

smtp.title: SMTP / Emails
smtp.desc: Sending notifications, order confirmations, and alerts. INSPECT ensures emails are dispatched and tracks delivery latencies.

stages.title: Stages analysis
stages.subtitle: How should we do when a single action launches multiple protocols at one time?
stages.desc: Key concept of INSPECT is the ability to track down a complete feature execution, even if it involves multiple protocols and services. If a user launch one http request, and that request makes an action in the database, INSPECT tracks the whole flow and show exactly what happened in a tab called 'Stages'. All chain is available to understand how it's organized.

user.title: User Experience & Journey Analytics
user.subtitle: Navigation and Product Analytics to maximize customer satisfaction
user.description: Technical performance only matters if it delivers value to the end user. INSPECT links navigation journeys directly to the real performance felt by your customers.

concept.title: What are User Journey and User Experience (UX) in a Web Application?
concept.desc: Understanding the sequence of user actions and their overall perception when interacting with the application.

journey.title: User Journey
journey.desc: Refers to the sequence of steps, screens, and actions (clicks, inputs, navigations) that a user performs to achieve a goal (e.g., logging in, searching for a file, submitting a form).

ux.title: User Experience (UX)
ux.desc: Encompasses the user's overall feeling: fluidity, display speed, workflow clarity, and the absence of errors or technical roadblocks.

role.title: INSPECT's Role in Navigation and User Experience
role.subtitle: In many architectures, when a user encounters an anomaly or slowdown, it is difficult to know exactly what they did. INSPECT bridges this gap by directly linking browser-side behavior to backend executions:

router.title: Router lifecycle monitoring (navigation.monitor.ts)
router.desc: INSPECT detects every URL change (NavigationStart, NavigationEnd, NavigationCancel) and timestamps transition durations.

cache.title: Advanced behavior handling
cache.desc: Support for browser Back-Forward Cache (pageshow / bfcache) and page unload events (beforeunload).

session.title: Session correlation (SessionManager)
session.desc: Each view or navigation is linked to a logical session, propagating technical IDs to backend HTTP requests.

dom.title: DOM (Document Object Model) event listening
dom.desc: The UserActionMonitor module automatically listens to DOM events, which are all basic user actions like click, scroll, and load.

semantic.title: Intelligent resolution
semantic.desc: INSPECT identifies target elements without manual setup by extracting labels via technical attributes.

error.title: Direct link to anomalies
error.desc: Any crash or network latency is instantly tied to the exact action and page where the user was.

analytics.title: The "Product Analytics (Beta)" Module in INSPECT
analytics.subtitle: The Product Analytics module transforms technical traces into an actionable visual timeline:

timeline.title: User Journey Timeline
timeline.desc: By selecting a user and a date, technical or support teams access the exact session replay as a chronological feed ("Page load", "Click on Submit button", "Field change").

reproduction.title: Ultra-Fast Incident Reproduction
reproduction.desc: No need to ask users to describe their steps, the scenario is easily reproduced.

insights.title: Understanding Real Usage
insights.desc: Enables product and development teams to identify most frequented paths, neglected screens.

intro.subtitle: Track transactions from the user click down to the database
intro.description: In modern multi-service architectures, following the path of an operation can be daunting. INSPECT provides continuous, seamless visibility across the entire chain.

cartography.title: Cartography
cartography.desc: You can retrieve the real graph of interactions, even after modifications in your code that hasn't been updated in documentation yet.

traceability.title: End-to-End Traceability
traceability.desc: You can retrieve the exact sequence of an operation (steps, durations, executed requests...).

tree.title: Detailed Trace Tree
tree.subtitle: Component-by-call view: An X-ray of your transactions
tree.description: The trace tree decomposes an operation into a visual hierarchy showing every component involved, each step's duration, and the exact failure point.

concept.title: Understanding the Trace Tree
concept.desc: A trace tree is like an itemized receipt or a family tree of execution: the parent action triggers child sub-actions.

span.title: Traces & Spans
span.desc: A trace represents the complete journey of a request. Each sub-step (database call, calculation, external request) is an accurately timed 'span'.

hierarchy.title: Hierarchical View
hierarchy.desc: A clean visual tree showing how components execute sequentially or concurrently.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Pinpoint the failing line of code in 3 clicks

first.title: Ultra-fast MTTR (Mean Time to Resolution)
first.desc: No need to read thousands of obscure log lines: the trace tree highlights the exact failing call in bright red.

second.title: Understand latency breakdown
second.desc: See at a glance if a 3-second operation spent 2.8 seconds waiting for a third-party response.

third.title: Bridging business and engineering
third.desc: A universal visual representation that allows business analysts to clearly point out failing steps to engineers.

thread.title: Thread Processing & Tracking
thread.subtitle: Asynchronism & Multi-threading: Never lose the thread
thread.description: To achieve high performance, modern applications distribute work across multiple virtual 'workers' (threads) running concurrently. INSPECT maintains unbroken traceability across thread boundaries.

concept.title: What are Threads and Asynchronism?
concept.desc: Simple explanations to understand how servers handle multiple tasks at once.

thread.title: What is a Thread?
thread.desc: A thread is an autonomous execution worker. Think of a restaurant kitchen brigade: each chef is a thread preparing a specific recipe alongside others.

async.title: What is Asynchronism?
async.desc: Delegating a heavy task to the background (e.g. generating a PDF report) and immediately freeing the user with an order buzzer without freezing their screen.

context.title: The Common Pitfall: Context Loss
context.desc: In most tools, when a task hops to a background worker, the correlation thread is lost. INSPECT solves this by seamlessly propagating the Trace ID.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Unbroken traceability even in complex async architectures

first.title: Full tracking of background tasks
first.desc: Follow transactions through message queues, background executors, and reactive pipelines.

second.title: Detection of thread locks (Deadlocks)
second.desc: Identify situations where workers wait on each other indefinitely, causing application freezes.

third.title: Native support for modern standards
third.desc: Compatible with standard threads and modern Virtual Threads (Java 21 Loom) with zero complex setup.

cartography.title: Global Architecture Map
cartography.subtitle: Dynamic real-time mapping of systems and dependencies
cartography.description: Say goodbye to outdated PowerPoint architecture diagrams. INSPECT automatically draws a living, real-time map of your system based on actual traffic.

concept.title: Understanding Dynamic Cartography
concept.desc: Dynamic cartography is the interactive, always up-to-date subway map of your software ecosystem.

map.title: The Flow Map (The Information Highway Map)
map.desc: A graphical diagram where each node is an application, service, or database, and each line reflects live communication.

health.title: Live Health Status (Traffic Color Codes)
health.desc: Nodes and connections change color (green, yellow, red) depending on live saturation and error rates.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Simplified governance and risk management

first.title: Always up-to-date documentation
first.desc: Get the true map of your architecture without relying on manual diagrams that quickly become obsolete.

second.title: Impact analysis before changes
second.desc: Before modifying or deprecating a service, instantly visualize every upstream application depending on it.

third.title: Clear communication with stakeholders
third.desc: Present the state of your infrastructure clearly and visually to leadership and audit committees.

intro.title: Proactive performance and health monitoring
intro.subtitle: Measure, anticipate, and guarantee service quality
intro.description: APM (Application Performance Monitoring) continuously measures the vitality of your software to detect performance degradations before users suffer.

sla.title: Health & Availability
sla.subtitle: SLA, Uptime, Error Rates, and Error Budgets
sla.description: Objectively measure compliance with service commitments and the reliability of your applications for customers and partners.

concept.title: Understanding availability and SLA concepts
concept.desc: Simple terms to measure if a service performs as promised.

sla.title: What is an SLA? (The Quality Commitment)
sla.desc: Service Level Agreement: The formal commitment of uptime (e.g., 99.9% guaranteed monthly availability).

uptime.title: What is Uptime? (Active Service Time)
uptime.desc: The percentage of time an application is accessible and fully operational without outages.

budget.title: What is an Error Budget? (The Safety Cushion)
budget.desc: The maximum number of incidents or minutes of downtime tolerated over a period before breaching contracts.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Ensure customer trust with verifiable metrics

first.title: Objective compliance reporting
first.desc: Generate reliable reports proving adherence to SLAs for clients and business partners.

second.title: Proactive alerts before SLA breach
second.desc: Get notified the moment error rates spike, well before your error budget is exhausted.

third.title: Data-driven service reviews
third.desc: Provide indisputable figures during quarterly performance reviews with business leaders.

performance.title: Performance & Response Times
performance.subtitle: Latency, Percentiles (P95, P99), and Bottlenecks
performance.description: Understand the true speed experienced by your users and uncover sneaky slowdowns hidden behind simple averages.

concept.title: Understanding latency and percentiles
concept.desc: Why averages can be misleading and how to measure true user experience.

latency.title: What is Latency? (The Waiting Time)
latency.desc: The delay between when a user clicks and when the response appears on screen.

percentile.title: Why Averages Lie: Percentiles (P95, P99)
percentile.desc: If 99 people wait 1s and 1 person waits 60s, the average looks decent. The P99 percentile reveals the reality of that slowest user.

bottleneck.title: What is a Bottleneck? (The Funnel)
bottleneck.desc: The specific component (database, network, heavy computation) slowing down the whole chain, like a lane closure on a highway.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Eliminate slowdowns frustrating your users

first.title: Detect isolated performance drops
first.desc: Spot the 1% or 5% of users experiencing unacceptable load times even when averages seem fine.

second.title: Surgical bottleneck identification
second.desc: Instantly pinpoint the component causing overall transaction delays.

third.title: Track optimization gains
third.desc: Immediately measure the impact of engineering optimizations on live user responsiveness.

volume.title: Volume & Throughput
volume.subtitle: Overall load, request throughput, and traffic spikes
volume.description: Track the volume of transactions processed per second and anticipate traffic spikes to ensure seamless service.

concept.title: Understanding throughput and load
concept.desc: Measuring your systems' ability to absorb customer activity.

rps.title: What is Throughput? (The Traffic Flow)
rps.desc: The number of requests, orders, or transactions successfully processed per time unit (e.g. 2,000 requests/sec).

spike.title: What is a Load Peak? (Rush Hour)
spike.desc: Moments of surge traffic (Black Friday sales, ticketing releases, monthly accounting closing).

capacity.title: Capacity Planning (Future-proofing)
capacity.desc: Anticipating traffic growth and scaling resources before infrastructure saturation occurs.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Prepare your infrastructure for high-stakes business events

first.title: Accurate infrastructure sizing
first.desc: Avoid overpaying for unnecessary cloud servers or undersizing machines using real load data.

second.title: Anticipate capacity limits
second.desc: Detect traffic growth trends weeks in advance to adjust server capacity comfortably.

third.title: Peace of mind during peak events
third.desc: Monitor live application behavior in real-time during product launches and promotional sales.

resources.title: System & Machine Resources
resources.subtitle: CPU consumption, JVM Memory, Active Threads, and Garbage Collector
resources.description: Monitor the physical health of machines hosting your software to prevent hardware crashes and memory leaks.

concept.title: Understanding system resources
concept.desc: The essential hardware elements powering your software applications.

cpu.title: The CPU (The Brain & Computing Power)
cpu.desc: The processor executing calculations. A CPU running at 100% slows down every application on that server.

ram.title: RAM / JVM Memory (The Desk Workspace)
ram.desc: The space where active data is held. If memory fills up (Out of Memory), the application immediately crashes.

gc.title: The Garbage Collector (Clearing the Desk)
gc.desc: The automated mechanism freeing unused memory. If it takes too long to clean, it causes noticeable micro-pauses.

threads.title: Active Threads (Working Hands)
threads.desc: The count of concurrent tasks currently executing on the machine.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Prevent hardware outages before services stop

first.title: Early warning on memory leaks
first.desc: Detect steadily creeping memory usage before it triggers an application crash.

second.title: Cloud cost optimization
second.desc: Right-size server instances based on actual resource consumption to lower cloud bills.

third.title: Continuous service stability
third.desc: Ensure maximum uptime by flagging overloaded nodes before they buckle under traffic.

intro.title: Application governance and deployment control
intro.subtitle: Real-time inventory and lifecycle event correlation
intro.description: Knowing exactly what version of software is running where and correlating issues with recent deployments is key to serene operations.

inventory.title: Application Inventory
inventory.subtitle: Complete inventory of your application estate by environment
inventory.description: A consolidated, live view of all your applications organized by environment (Development, Staging, Pre-production, Production).

concept.title: Understanding application inventory
concept.desc: The comprehensive and live record of all software assets across your company.

environments.title: Environments (The Validation Stages)
environments.desc: Dev (coding), Staging (testing), Pre-prod (qualification), and Production (live customers).

versioning.title: Version Governance (The Release Numbers)
versioning.desc: Knowing whether version 2.4.1 or 2.4.0 is deployed on each server to prevent discrepancies.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: No more doubts about what is running on your servers

first.title: Instant visibility across the whole estate
first.desc: Find all deployed modules across the enterprise in a few clicks without bothering system administrators.

second.title: Detect version drift
second.desc: Immediately spot if a production server was missed during a security patch rollout.

third.title: Simplified audits and compliance
third.desc: Provide exact lists of running software during security reviews and governance audits.

events.title: Lifecycle Events History
events.subtitle: Restarts, version upgrades, deployments, and unexpected stops
events.description: Keep a historical record of every major lifecycle event to instantly correlate a technical change with its performance impact.

concept.title: Understanding lifecycle events
concept.desc: Any event that modifies the operational state of an application over time.

deployments.title: Deployments (Going Live)
deployments.desc: The exact moment a new software version is installed and activated.

restarts.title: Restarts (Planned or Accidental)
restarts.desc: Knowing whether a server restarted due to planned maintenance or an unexpected crash.

correlation.title: Temporal Correlation (Cause and Effect)
correlation.desc: Chronologically linking a sudden spike in errors to a deployment made 5 minutes earlier.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Know immediately what changed in your systems

first.title: Instant regression identification
first.desc: If error rates jump after a 2 PM release, INSPECT immediately highlights the causal deployment link.

second.title: Informed rollback decisions
second.desc: Empowers managers to quickly decide on rolling back a release before customer impact escalates.

third.title: Continuous stability auditing
third.desc: Track unexpected restart frequencies to identify fundamentally unstable services.

intro.title: Zero administrative overhead and intelligent self-management
intro.subtitle: An autonomous system that self-optimizes, self-purges, and self-monitors
intro.description: Adopting an observability tool should never increase administrative burden. INSPECT autonomously manages its storage, database, and operational resilience.

partitioning.title: Dynamic Data Partitioning
partitioning.subtitle: Automatic creation of Day/Month partitions without human intervention
partitioning.description: To remain blazing fast even with billions of records, INSPECT automatically organizes data into chronological compartments.

concept.title: What is Data Partitioning?
concept.desc: An essential technique to ensure search queries remain lightning fast over time.

partition.title: The Partition Concept (Monthly Filing Cabinets)
partition.desc: Instead of throwing every document into a giant 10-meter-high box, you maintain a folder per day or month. Searches only look in the target folder.

dynamic.title: Dynamic Automation (Zero Manual Work)
dynamic.desc: INSPECT automatically generates upcoming partitions ahead of time without needing database administrators (DBAs).

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Constant performance with zero database maintenance

first.title: Instant search performance year-round
first.desc: Query a 3-month-old trace just as quickly as a trace recorded 5 seconds ago.

second.title: Zero DBA administrative cost
second.desc: Your database teams do not need to write or maintain partition maintenance scripts.

third.title: Limitless scalability
third.desc: Easily accommodates massive data volumes without ever saturating storage access.

retention.title: Smart Retention & Purge
retention.subtitle: Distributed configuration and differentiated retention: Technical vs Functional
retention.description: Optimize storage costs by keeping short-lived technical traces for diagnostics and long-term functional business records for audits and compliance.

concept.title: Understanding differentiated retention and purge
concept.desc: Keep the right level of information without wasting expensive disk space.

retention.title: What is Retention? (Storage Duration)
retention.desc: The policy determining how many days records are kept before automated cleanup.

differentiated.title: Differentiated Retention (Tech vs Business)
differentiated.desc: Keep heavy microsecond technical spans for 7 to 14 days, while preserving business transactions for 6 to 12 months.

purge.title: Smart Purge (Automated Cleanup)
purge.desc: Instantly and cleanly dropping expired partition tables in milliseconds without CPU spikes.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Storage cost control and regulatory compliance

first.title: Substantial disk storage savings
first.desc: Prevent disk bloat by automatically pruning heavy, expired technical spans.

second.title: Regulatory compliance (GDPR & Audits)
second.desc: Meet data retention rules reliably without risking compliance oversights.

third.title: Simple centralized rules
third.desc: Define retention policies per module and let INSPECT enforce them automatically.

reporting.title: Collector Self-Reporting
reporting.subtitle: Embedded anomaly reporting and circuit-breaker safety
reporting.description: Who watches the watcher? INSPECT agents continuously self-diagnose and protect host applications from any performance impact.

concept.title: Understanding Self-Reporting and resilience
concept.desc: The guarantee that observability will never slow down or crash your business applications.

report.title: What is Self-Reporting? (Self-Diagnosis)
report.desc: The INSPECT agent's ability to measure its own resource usage and report transmission backpressure.

circuit.title: Circuit-Breaker (The Safety Fuse)
circuit.desc: Just like a circuit breaker in your home: if the backend is saturated, the agent temporarily throttles collection to protect 100% of the host app's CPU and RAM.

value.title: The INSPECT Advantage for Your Teams
value.subtitle: Complete peace of mind for production operations

first.title: Guaranteed zero-impact in production
first.desc: INSPECT will never consume critical resources during high-traffic crisis situations.

second.title: Total operational transparency
second.desc: Inspect the health of collectors and data transmission queues at any time.

third.title: Self-healing and seamless recovery
third.desc: Automatically resumes full telemetry transmission once backend capacity normalizes.

installation.title: Installation
installation.content: To install INSPECT, there are 2 dependencies to add to your project: INSPECT-core and INSPECT-ng-collector

function.title: Function
function.jakarta: API used for the email management

collector.title: Collector
collector.content: The collector is the component responsible for collecting data from various sources. It can collect data from logs, metrics, and traces, and send them to the server for processing and storage.

server.title: Server
server.content: The server is the component responsible for processing and storing the data collected by the collector. It also provides a user interface for visualizing and analyzing the collected data, allowing users to understand the performance and behavior of their application.

components.title: Technical components
components.content: INSPECT is composed of several technical components that work together to provide a comprehensive monitoring and analysis solution. These components include the collector, server, and application, as well as various libraries and tools that facilitate data collection, processing, and visualization.
